skill.name: wp-playground
skill.description: Guides WordPress Playground workflows for disposable WordPress sites, local CLI servers, blueprints, snapshots, version switching, and Xdebug debugging.
skill.summary: Guide WordPress Playground setup, blueprints, snapshots, version testing, and Xdebug workflows.
skill.author: Automattic

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples or official WordPress URLs and are false positives for command execution or suspicious networking. Real concerns remain around unpinned npx execution, remote Blueprint inputs, and flags that can let Blueprints read adjacent local files. No prompt injection evidence found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin @wp-playground/cli to a known version or ask for confirmation before using @latest.
Tell users to run only trusted Blueprints and review steps that run PHP or modify files.
Use --blueprint-may-read-adjacent-files only for reviewed local assets and never with untrusted Blueprint sources.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Blueprint Execution Risk
semantic_findings.description: The blueprint reference lists runPHP, applyPatches, and writeFile steps, while the skill supports remote Blueprint URLs and adjacent file reads. Untrusted Blueprints could execute PHP or read local files when risky flags are enabled.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly document executable and file-modifying Blueprint steps plus a CLI flag that allows local adjacent file reads. The risk depends on accepting untrusted Blueprint sources, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Local WordPress testing often needs fast setup, clean state, and version control. This skill guides Playground CLI and browser workflows for blueprints, snapshots, debugging, and compatibility checks.
actual_capabilities: Start a local WordPress Playground server with auto-mounted plugin or theme code.
Run Blueprint files or URLs with WordPress and PHP version options.
Build shareable site snapshots from reviewed Blueprint recipes.
Guide Xdebug setup for plugin and theme debugging.
Use Playground URLs for browser-only preview and sharing workflows.
Troubleshoot mounts, ports, Node version issues, and slow runs.
limitations: Requires Node.js 20.18 or newer for local CLI workflows.
Does not replace a full WordPress stack when native database access is required.
Should not run untrusted Blueprint URLs or ZIP files without review.
Ephemeral Playground instances are not suitable for production data.

use_cases.title: Test Plugin Changes Locally
use_cases.description: Mount a plugin into Playground, verify activation, and check behavior across WordPress or PHP versions.

use_cases.title: Preview Theme Compatibility
use_cases.description: Launch a disposable site, install a theme, and compare behavior across target WordPress releases.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reproducible Bug Reports
use_cases.description: Build a reviewed Blueprint or snapshot that recreates a reported issue for triage.

prompt_templates.title: Start Local Playground
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wp-playground skill to start a disposable WordPress Playground for my plugin. Check prerequisites, mount the project, and list verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wp-playground skill to review and run this Blueprint source. Explain required trust checks before execution and summarize the expected setup.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Compatibility Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wp-playground skill to reproduce this WordPress issue with a pinned WordPress and PHP version. Include Xdebug setup and smoke tests.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Shareable Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wp-playground skill to design a reviewed Blueprint workflow, build a shareable snapshot, and document verification for CI or bug triage.

output_examples.input: I need to test a plugin without installing a full WordPress stack.
output: The response recommends checking Node version, starting a Playground server with auto-mount, and verifying the plugin is active.
It lists version options and simple smoke tests.

output_examples.input: I have a Blueprint for a demo site and need a shareable artifact.
output: The response reviews the Blueprint source, warns about untrusted URLs, and recommends a snapshot workflow.
It explains how to confirm installed themes, plugins, and site state before sharing.

output_examples.input: Breakpoints do not hit while debugging a theme.
output_examples.output: The response checks Xdebug startup flags, IDE port settings, path mappings, and Playground mount paths.

best_practices: Pin CLI, WordPress, and PHP versions when results must be reproducible.
Review Blueprint sources before running them, especially when they use remote URLs.
Keep mounted projects free of secrets and production data.
anti_patterns: Do not mount broad home directories or folders that contain secrets.
Do not use public Blueprint URLs from sources you do not trust.
Do not treat Playground results as proof for production infrastructure behavior.

faq.question: Can this skill run WordPress without Docker?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides WordPress Playground workflows that run WordPress through WebAssembly and SQLite.

faq.question: Does it support local plugin and theme testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains auto-mount and explicit mount options for plugin and theme projects.

faq.question: Can I use browser-only Playground links?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers fragment and query URL workflows for quick previews and shared blueprints.

faq.question: Is it safe to run any Blueprint URL?
faq.answer: No. Review remote Blueprints first because they can install packages, run PHP, and modify files.

faq.question: Does it help with debugging?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines Xdebug setup, path mappings, and verification checks.

faq.question: When should I avoid Playground?
faq.answer: Avoid it for production data, native database requirements, or features that need unavailable PHP extensions.
